name: evitan/plus
description: Evitan Plus — offline-first retail point of sale desktop app (Laravel + React + NativePHP + SQLite).

scripts-descriptions.verify: Run every release gate, fail-fast, cheapest first: composer audit, pint, phpstan, backend tests, tsc, eslint, prettier, Playwright e2e. The audit step needs network; abandoned packages are ignored because nativephp/electron and nativephp/laravel are deliberate pins.
scripts-descriptions.verify:console: Run the provisioning console's WHOLE test suite, Unit and Feature. Needs (cd console && composer install) first plus CONSOLE_DB_* in console/.env pointing at the live Supabase project, which is why this is separate from `verify` rather than part of it — `verify` has to stay runnable offline and without admin credentials. --fail-on-skipped is the honesty guard: Tests\TestCase skips silently without credentials, so without the flag a misconfigured console/.env exits 0 having tested nothing. That is exactly how SchemaParityTest sat unrun from M1 to M4.
scripts-descriptions.rig: Dev-only, not a gate: run TWO browser instances of the app as two branches of one throwaway business, to look at the product from a user's seat without rebuilding an AppImage. Provisions a real business + 2 branches on the live Supabase project, seeds a catalog with different stock per branch, four accounts (owner/admin/cashier1/cashier2, all password `password`) and A YEAR of sales ending today — MNL busier than CEB — hydrates both local SQLite databases, and serves them at 127.0.0.1:8131 and 127.0.0.2:8132. The year is what makes /reports, the consolidated per-branch table and deep pagination worth opening; the cost is that a branch which has sold something has no opening window, so M13.5's opening-stock import is only reachable from `rig:wizard`. Two different loopback HOSTS rather than two ports on one: the XSRF-TOKEN cookie name is hardcoded in the framework and cookies are host-scoped, not port-scoped, so two ports would poison each other's CSRF token and every submit would bounce with 'your session expired'. Runs in the foreground; Ctrl-C destroys everything it made, including the Postgres schema and both branch roles. Needs network, console/.env, and `npm run build` first.
scripts-descriptions.rig:wizard: As `rig`, but stops before hydrating: both devices come up un-hydrated on /setup and the banner prints the two credentials JSON paths for you to type into the wizard by hand — which is the only way to see that screen as a user meets it. The wizard takes a filesystem PATH, not an upload, and there is no Browse button outside the desktop runtime, so the paths are printed absolute. It also seeds NO sales, deliberately: a branch that has never sold anything still has its opening window (`OpeningWindow::isOpen()`), so this is the mode that can show the opening-stock import. Same catalog, stock and four accounts as `rig`.
scripts-descriptions.rig:clean: The safety net for a rig that was killed before its Ctrl-C teardown could run. Reads tests/manual/.runtime/state.env — written incrementally as each artifact is created, and carrying the SCHEMA name from before the provision call rather than after it, so it is accurate even after a kill -9 during provisioning — and destroys exactly what that one run made: its servers, SQLite files, credential JSONs, schema and roles. Nothing global, and no sweep over biz_%: such a schema is indistinguishable from a real customer's, which is why there is no reaper (console/README.md §5). With NO state file it runs `pg.php orphans`, which PRINTS every biz_ schema that never finished provisioning — no completed audit row, no branches row, no schema_meta — and the drop line to run; a schema mid-build in a concurrent suite looks the same from there, so a human decides. If the Postgres drop fails it prints the SQL and KEEPS the state file and both credential JSONs, because deleting them is the only way to lose a schema name for good.
scripts-descriptions.rig:clean:all: Everything `rig:clean` does, then a sweep of every DISPOSABLE schema — `biz_test_*`, the namespace `business:provision --disposable` puts throwaway businesses in and that SchemaName::forBusiness() cannot otherwise produce. That is what separates this from the reaper the paragraph above refuses to be: it is not a guess about a `biz_%` name, it is a namespace no real business can enter, whatever its actor, business name or branch code. It sweeps what the rig, `verify:console` and `verify:hydrate` leave behind when a run dies before its teardown, including runs that left no state file at all — the mark is the schema NAME, so it exists from CREATE SCHEMA onward and survives a kill -9 that never got as far as an audit row. Refuses outright if pgrep finds a phpunit or another rig running, because those suites hold disposable schemas for the length of a test class; that check only sees this machine. No transaction-count guard: a rig business has a year of seeded sales in it.

dev: npx concurrently -c "#93c5fd,#c4b5fd,#fb7185,#fdba74" "php artisan serve" "php artisan queue:listen --tries=1" "php artisan pail --timeout=0" "npm run dev" --names=server,queue,logs,vite
native:dev: npx concurrently -k -c "#93c5fd,#c4b5fd" "php artisan native:serve --no-interaction" "npm run dev" --names=app,vite
